claims.text: A hybrid TOR-TILD and machine-learning interatomic-potential approach can improve thermodynamic-property determination for multicomponent high-entropy materials at high temperatures.
The proposed intervention is to combine TOR-TILD with machine-learning interatomic potentials.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can efficiently sample the large compositional space of multicomponent high-entropy materials.
TOR-TILD supplies accuracy for critical thermodynamic properties within the hybrid approach.
The hybrid approach can treat both solid and dense-fluid phases around the transition.
The hybrid approach can retain ab initio-level accuracy.
The hybrid approach will improve the accuracy of transition-temperature determination relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The hybrid approach will improve the accuracy of fusion-enthalpy and fusion-entropy determination relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The hybrid approach will improve the accuracy of transition volume-change determination relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The hybrid approach will improve the accuracy of dense-fluid heat-capacity determination relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The hybrid approach will be more computationally efficient than existing DFT free-energy and TOR-TILD methods.
The approach is applicable only within composition and temperature domains for which it can be trained and validated.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials may not transfer reliably across diverse high-entropy-material compositions.
TOR-TILD calculations may incur errors for complex multicomponent systems.
